ships.name: Akousnikis
ships.description: The Akousnikis is a composite freighter constructed from the salvaged wreckage of a Akoustiki and a pair of Sonikis. Despite being smaller than an Avlaki, its compact design has made it both tougher and more difficult to hit.

ships.name: Avlakinos
ships.description: Bolting two additional cargo pods to the front of an Avlaki resulted in a variant known as the Avlakinos. The additional weight is most noticeable when the cargo pods are full. 	Although this modification is reversible, captains who have gone through the process rarely change their minds later.

ships.name: Modified Frequentia
ships.description: The discovery of Gossamer caused many to look at the Frequentia-class freighter as the optimal choice for hauling the fish found there. But the lack of any weapon mounts to harvest them proved to be an obstacle to this purpose. 	With your Avgi Harvester license, and a modest markup to cover labor costs, the shipyard is willing to add a single turret mount to solve this issue.

ships.name: Optulon
ships.description: The Optulon is a composite interceptor constructed from the salvaged wreckage of an Optikon and an Undulon. It is normally outfitted for deep space excursions to hunt aberrant. It is able to record and transmit sensor data on the aberrant it encounters, but this is a secondary concern.

ships.name: Phonikos
ships.description: The Phonikos is a composite interceptor constructed from the salvaged wreckage of a Photikon and a Sonikis. Enough space to accomodate a single pilot remains after disposing of the wrecked computers and redundant equipment. 	Despite the dangers imposed by the Incursion, there are Avgi willing to pilot a fragile vessel such as this for the freedom it provides to visit other worlds. This has made it a popular starter ship for Dissonant pirates.

ships.name: Sonikikis
ships.description: The Sonikikis is a larger sized Utility Drone that requires the use of a fighter bay to house it. This has limited it to a niche role in deep space mining operations. Offering double the cargo space of a Sonikis, it can be slow when carrying a full load. 	Fighters do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a fighter unless you have a ship in your fleet with a fighter bay.

ships.name: Tremoferos
ships.description: The Tremoferos is a composite Frigate constructed from the salvaged wreckage of a Tremoros and an Interferos. Enough space to accomodate a small crew remains after disposing of the wrecked computers and redundant equipment.

ships.name: Interlari
ships.description: The Interlari is a composite Frigate constructed from the salvaged wreckage of an Interferos and a Polari. A new experimental Lamina is installed on it...

ships.name: Poloptikon
ships.description: The Poloptikon is a composite Scout constructed from the salvaged wreckage of a Polari and two Optikons. A new experimental Lamina is installed on it...

ships.name: Polipolari
ships.description: The Polipolari is a composite Scout constructed from the salvaged wreckage of two Polaris. A new experimental Lamina is installed on it...

ships.name: Kimek Bramble
ships.description: The Bramble is a recent addition to Kimek fleets, giving them a viable option for transporting large amounts of time sensitive freight.

ships.name: Saryd Trailblazer
ships.description: The Trailblazer is the ancient warship Coalition shipyards are referring to during their sales pitch for the Sojourner. These relics of war are no longer in production. Of the few known to still exist, most are kept as display pieces in private collections. It is a rare sight to see one in actual use.

ships.name: Fulgur
ships.description: The Fulgur is the most advanced ship produced by the Ignitia. It features the most heat resistant hull their shipyards are capable of constructing, a necessity for ships constructed on Ignus.  This ship can land on the super heated environments of lava planets. Of course, this protection does not extend to any crew or passengers who disembark after landing...

ships.name: Judgement
ships.description: Judgement enforces the will of the Justicar Court beyond Jurisprudence.

ships.name: Witness Drone
ships.description: Witnesses provide testimony of the suspect's crimes. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay.

ships.name: Bailiff Drone
ships.description: Bailiffs facilitate enforcement of the court's judgement. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay.

ships.name: Worldcrusher
ships.description: The first vessel of its kind; and the last.

ships.name: Corpse Trickster
ships.description: Although it lacks the ability to travel through Hyperspace on its own, these parasitic predators evolved a means to control the bodily functions of a dead Subsidurial by thrusting its tentacles into the nervous system of the corpse. After doing so, it is able to use the Subsidurial's ability to traverse across Hyperspace. 	Corpse Tricksters also have the ability to create hypnotic illusions, though the means by which it accomplishes this are a mystery. A favored tactic is creating an image of a Subsidurial to lure a fresh host. Alternatively, it might make multiple images of itself to intimidate and confuse other predators.

ships.name: Pincer Beast
ships.description: This creature appears to have an outer shell made of small asteroids held together by strands of carbon nanotubes. It pulls rocks through arms into its main cavity where it processes them to make more shell. The multi-colored hairs pointing back seem to be a drive system of sorts, manipulating the gravity field around the creature to accelerate it. There is no apparent hyperdrive mechanism, but somehow it is able to open a hyperspace window.

ships.name: Star Gazer
ships.description: An invasive species from beyond our galaxy. They seem possessed by an insatiable curiosity, observing everything they encounter with multiple eyes and other, more alien, sensory organs. While not particularly aggressive, Stargazers can be dangerous if provoked. Their bodies are covered with sharp quills that can be flung towards predators. They regenerate quickly, allowing them to maintain a constant stream of fire. These projectiles are made of a material that evades detection by anti-missile systems and may have other unknown properties.

ships.name: Unstable Wormhole
ships.description: These wormholes are too small for anything larger than a drone to fly through. The aperture is unstable and may shift locations, or collapse entirely, at any moment. The few drones that do make it through seem to have their programming scrambled, perhaps a result of the strange bolts of energy surrounding the phenomenon.

ships.name: Hyperspace Anomaly
ships.description: A phenomenon consisting of small tears in the fabric of reality briefly connecting normal space with hyperspace. The existence of these anomalies may provide some hint regarding the nature of wormholes and their creation.

ships.name: Genesis Spacecraft
ships.description: A basic space exploration vessel from a pre-hyperdrive civilization. The hull lacks any form of shield emitter and doesn't have the internal safety protocols found on the ships of more advanced species. But it does seem sturdier than the hull of an equivalently sized human ship.

ships.name: Buckler
ships.description: Built upon a Dagger chassis, the Buckler plays a very different combat role from its smaller sibling. Lacking any weapon mounts, it features a high number of shield emitters and some of the toughest hull armor of any interceptor in the galaxy. 	Buckler pilots are expected to prioritize the defense of the flagship they are meant to protect over their own safety. To encourage this, new Bucklers purchased from Lionheart include a free training video installed on the ship's computer. Mixed in with tutorials for operating and maintaining the spacecraft are inspirational stories praising heroic pilots who sacrificed themselves for the greater good.

ships.name: Deuterium Tanker
ships.description: Deuterium Tankers are slow and difficult to maneuver ships. They supply spaceports with hyperspace fuel from deuterium refineries. The vital service provided by them are an important element in the galactic economy that is rarely acknowledged. 	Inexperienced or foolish pirates sometimes mistake a Deuterium Tanker for a regular freighter with disastrous results. The contents of their high capacity fuel tanks creates a fiery hazard when the ship explodes, burning any ships caught in the blast. 	This ship has some resistance to fuel leaks.

ships.name: Pirate Drone
ships.description: Locals started making these in their backyard garages to satisfy a limited demand for unofficial combat drones. From a distance, it looks like someone duct taped an energy blaster to the side of a civilian science drone. Upon closer inspection, that assessment isn't too far off. Each drone has minor differences in construction materials and how the wires are routed. Few pirates actually use these, but the ones who do tend to buy them in bulk.

While some Stingrays can still be found protecting private merchant fleets or mining asteroids, many have found their way into the hands of pirates.

ships.name: Liberator
ships.description: The Liberator is a new warship that was originally designed by Southbound Shipyards to replace the Skein. Rumor has it that the project scope shifted focus during development when a ship of alien origin was discovered at the edges of the Rim. As a result, the planned fighter bays were scrapped in favor of the concentrated fire mount. This design crams all of the ship's gun ports into a single central location, allowing multiple smaller guns to emulate the effect of having a single larger one. This negatively impacts the ship's cooling efficiency and increases the amount of work maintenance crews have to put in for guns not mounted on the edge of the firing cluster.

ships.name: Mastodon

Only one Mastodon is still listed in active service on the Republic's official ship registry.

ships.name: War Hauler
ships.description: A leftover from the Alpha Wars, War Hauler production stopped soon after the wars ended. Although the ship predates the Republic and is not manufactured by any modern shipyards, Parliament still passed a law prohibiting retail sales of this ship to ordinary civilians. This has made the few remaining War Haulers on the secondary market a highly sought after item amongst collectors of antique ships.

ships.name: Metropolis
ships.description: Among the largest models of all city ships, a Metropolis is formed through the combination of three smaller utility ships. An emergency separation feature is supposed to allow the three ships to act independently. However, that feature is currently malfunctioning with this particular Metropolis ship. Perhaps one day, you will find an engineer who can figure out how to unfreeze the binding clamps without destroying the ship in the process.

ships.name: District
ships.description: The District ship comprises the aft portion of a Metropolis ship. It features the most outfit and cargo space of the three sections as well as the most weapons support. While it does not have a proper fighter bay, a small landing pad on the roof is outfitted with a docking port and clamps, allowing a support fighter to latch onto its back.

ships.name: Prefecture
ships.description: The Prefecture comprises the center portion of a Metropolis ship. It includes two fighter bays along with a good portion of cargo and outfit space. Four turrets provide a platform for offensive weaponry.

ships.name: Municipality
ships.description: The Municipality comprises the forward section of a Metropolis ship. It is the only section with forward firing gun ports. However, it has the least cargo and outfit space of the three sections. Special sensor equipment was integrated into the foremost part of the ship to aid in planetary exploration and mapping. One of its two fighter bays was modified to host a pair of drones.

ships.name: Starcadia
ships.description: The technology on the Starcadia, while in line with other modern ships, is surprisingly mundane for a newly deployed ship from the Deep. This has caused some to speculate that the Deep has lost their edge in technological advancement. Alternatively, conspiracy theorists suggest that the Deep has been sitting on this design for some time and is only releasing it now in preparation for some threat unknown to the general public. Deep Security, for its part, has no comment on these rumors.

ships.name: Marauder Argosy
ships.description: What was once a simple Argosy is buried beneath thick plates of additional hull armor and shield emitters. Reconfigured gun ports, expanded engine space, and a drone bay leave little room for cargo in this medium warship.

ships.name: Modified Hogshead
ships.description: Occasionally a pirate gets the idea in his head to adapt a ship not designed for warfare into a pirate vessel. Oftentimes the results weren't worth the effort. But some of these attempts manage to find a niche. A Modified Hogshead might appear under the command of bounty hunters or slavers who are likely to find a ship of this type useful in their line of work. 	Over half the passenger space on this Hogshead has been gutted to make room for more shield emitters and weapon systems to power the two additional gun ports. Thick armored plating has been welded over the passenger viewports and other vulnerable areas of the hull, making the ship heavier, but more durable.

ships.name: Arcus
ships.description: The Arcus is a hybrid transport-freighter designed for deep space exploration. It is intended to serve as the core upon which a colony station can be established and expanded upon. 	Merchant captains willing to pay the exhorbitant cost can employ this ship in mundane transport-freight operations.

ships.name: Castellanus
ships.description: The Castillanus heavy warship expands upon the design principles exhibited by the Nimbus. While it cannot match the raw offensive power of the Venta, the turret mounts make it a more versatile weapons platform.

ships.name: Nimbo Cumulus
ships.description: A recently developed upgrade to the Nimbo Stratus. With it's extra gun port and weapon capacity, some regard the Cumulus as a light warship. The Hicemus are closely monitoring how the ship performs to determine whether or not it needs to be placed under their licensing restrictions.

ships.name: Veliante'ixis
ships.description: Most Builder ships were destroyed by the Ka'het. Concealed for millennia under the ocean waves of Retilie, this warship survived the invasion. It was found by Lu Bu during the Grave Digger's exploration of the Graveyard. Lu Bu never completed salvage operations, but a few former Grave Diggers knew of the derelict's location.

ships.name: Kai'xeris
ships.description: Designed to haul cargo over short distances, the Kai'xeris is one of the few Builder ships not destroyed by the Ka'het. 	This ship is capable of diving into the harsh atmosphere of a gas giant.

ships.name: Kai'teris
ships.description: Designed to ferry passengers over short distances, the Kai'teris is one of the few Builder ships not destroyed by the Ka'het. 	This ship is capable of diving into the harsh atmosphere of a gas giant.

ships.name: Rao'xeris
ships.description: A deep space mining vessel, the Rao'xeris was used to transport materials harvested in the northern reaches of Builder space to processing facilities in the southern region. When the Ka'het invasion began, many found that it could easily be converted into a combat warship. 	This ship is capable of diving into the harsh atmosphere of a gas giant.

ships.name: Ool'mar
ships.description: Featuring the Builders' best ramscoop technology with integrated fuel stabilizers and storage tanks, the Ool'mar was specifically designed for the purpose of harvesting and transporting hyperspace fuel. With the collapse of the Builder civilization, there was no longer any need to harvest fuel. Most Ool'mar can be found wandering aimlessly, unable to off load the contents of their fuel tanks because Builder stations lack the capacity to accept their cargo. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay. 	This ship is capable of diving into the harsh atmosphere of a gas giant.

ships.name: Veliante'exis
ships.description: This is the only Builder ship that hasn't been completely destroyed by the Ka'het. Concealed for millennia under the ocean waves of Retilie, it was found by Lu Bu during the Grave Digger's exploration of the Graveyard. Lu Bu never completed salvage operations, but a few former Grave Diggers knew of the derelict's location. The ship's original outfits couldn't be salvaged. The Grave Diggers have replaced them with Ka'het outfits.

ships.name: Ancient Raider
ships.description: An old alien ship that was stolen from a Syndicate Shipyards lab.

ships.name: Akfir A'awoj
ships.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This utility vessel was converted into a warship early in the Korath civil war, but was quickly outclassed as the war intensified. It is named after a world that vanished from Korath space. Nir Akfir may still exist in the territory of another species. If it does, they probably refer to it by a different name.

ships.name: Far'itar
ships.description: Dedicated cargo transports are no longer necessary among the Korath Exiles. Rather than being scrapped, these ships have been repurposed to serve as mobile prisons. Criminals convicted of serious crimes are given a choice between a quick death via a microbot nutrigel processor or a life long assignment working on a Far'itar mining vessel. Prisoners who fail to perform their duties are still eligible for being tossed into the nutrigel processor. 	Operating these vessels can be lucrative for its captains, but the Korath authorities require them to activate their self destruct in the event of a mutiny or other event that could result in a prisoner escape. Whether or not they have the fortitude to fulfill this duty is put to the test whenever they engage in a boarding battle.

ships.name: Kar'iyar
ships.description: The Kar'iyar is a lightly armed fighter transport ship. They primarily serve as escorts to supplement the fire power of larger Korath fleets.

ships.name: Paragon Zibruka
ships.description: The Zibruka is the smallest Pug warship that you know of. It is a fearsome ship to face off against, especially in swarms. 	The Paragon variant of the Zibruka is intended for battles rated tier 2 and above. It has increased shielding and a reinforced hull. It also adds a turret mount and the additional space to use it.

ships.name: Paragon Enfolta
ships.description: The Enfolta is a medium-sized Pug warship. A single Enfolta can take on multiple smaller human ships. 	The Paragon variant of the Enfolta is intended for battles rated tier 2 and above. It has increased shielding and a reinforced hull. It also adds one more turret mount with the additional space to use it.

ships.name: Savage Zibruka
ships.description: The Zibruka is the smallest Pug warship that you know of. Despite having only two gun ports, its two advanced guns combined with its fast and efficient engine systems make it a fearsome ship to face off against, especially in swarms. 	The Savage variant of the Zibruka was originally designed to withstand harsh environments. The bio regenerative hull is resistant to corrosion, heat, and ion damage.

ships.name: Savage Enfolta
ships.description: The Enfolta is a medium-sized Pug warship. It has a formidable armament of advanced weaponry supported by powerful integrated energy generation. A single Enfolta can take on multiple smaller human ships. 	The Savage variant of the Enfolta was originally designed to withstand harsh environments. The bio regenerative hull is resistant to corrosion, heat, and ion damage.

ships.name: Savage Maboro
ships.description: The Maboro appears to be the Pug's capital warship. Its shield matrix and hull are much weaker than human capital ships; however, it is able to regenerate its shields quickly. Its fearsome ordnance and advanced anti-missile defenses make it a ship that only the strongest human capital ships are able to oppose. 	The Savage variant of the Maboro was originally designed to withstand harsh environments. The bio regenerative hull is resistant to corrosion, heat, and ion damage.

ships.name: Ghost Zibruka

The Ghost variant of the Zibruka is intended for covert observation and surveillance. It has cloaking integrated into the hull.

ships.description: Typhons are old freighters the Quarg use mostly to transport materials in bulk.

ships.name: Quarg Zahhak
ships.description: The Zahhak is a Quarg utility support ship for extended deep space operations.

ships.name: Quarg Naga
ships.description: The Naga was a mining vessel dating back to the pre-ringworld era.

ships.name: Quarg Skycrane
ships.description: Based on a heavy freighter frame with expanded capabilities, the Skycrane is a utility ship used by the Quarg for a variety of purposes.

ships.name: Quarg Skythrush
ships.description: The Skythrush was designed to be used as a blockade runner. Over a thousand years have passed since anyone has dared lay siege to the Quarg, shifting their role towards cargo support and scouting.

ships.name: Quarg Warkite
ships.description: The Warkite is a nimble assault ship used by the Quarg to harass and break enemy fleet formations or make quick surgical strikes against targets behind enemy lines.

ships.name: Quarg Warwyrm
ships.description: The Warwyrm is used by the Quarg as a heavy warship. Slow to deploy due to their low fuel capacity, they are rarely seen outside of their planetary defense fleets.

ships.name: Quarg Skyshrew
ships.description: The Skyshrew is a fighter that can provide fire support to Quarg ships with the bays to carry them. An array of essential non-weapon systems are built into the hull.

ships.name: Ember Nightmare
ships.description: An abomination constructed by adding the salvaged remains of destroyed Remnant ships to what was originally an Albatross. Beelzebub has had this ship since abandoning the Remnant in pursuit of his own fortunes amongst the pirates of the ancestral humans.

ships.name: Modified Bactrian
ships.description: The owner of this Bactrian has replaced some of it's armored hull plating with additional shield emitters. This has made the ship lighter and faster. An additional fighter can be carried on a landing pad on the roof.

ships.name: Nightingale
ships.description: The Nightingale is a drone developed for long-term survillance over the uninhabited systems of the Ember Waste. They are fragile constructs built more for stealth than combat.

ships.name: Prefect's Albatross
ships.description: Once they left human space, it became apparent to the Remnant that they would need to build their own shipyards in order to defend themselves if they were discovered by the Alphas or any other unfriendly faction. Using new composite materials that they discovered, they built ships very different from anything seen in human space. The wings of this Albatross sweep back, giving it a sleek appearance. This marks it as a Prefect's Albatross, used on the rare occasion when a Prefect isn't riding on a cloaked ship.

ships.name: Raptor Prototype
ships.description: The Raptor Prototype is the result of experiments utilizing biological specimens collected from across the galaxy and beyond. As a result, its design is a bit different from other Remnant ships.

ships.name: Shrike
ships.description: The Shrike is a nimble gunship that is usually outfitted to provide long distance fire support. Remnant captains embarking on solo missions might opt for a more aggressive outfit selection instead.

ships.description: A lightly armed escort ship used by the Sheragi to accompany their cargo and transport fleets.

ships.name: Diamondback
ships.description: Diamondbacks have been in use since explorers first settled the galactic rim. They've fought in various wars throughout the centuries and few survive to this day. Those that have are so extensively customized that no two are alike. Some southern legends claim the Diamondbacks were wrecked spacecraft created by extinct aliens and salvaged by early explorers such as Han Sizer. There is no evidence to support these claims and no reputable scholar takes them seriously.

ships.name: Kvelqde-Sosrue
ships.description: This Kvelqde variant is designed to optimize the use of "Myiara" Fire Spouts. There are whispers that those who pilot such vessels are patron servants of a secret House that manipulates events from the shadows. Within the respectable echelons of Successor society such tales are dismissed as mere superstition, no more real than the monster from a children's poem. 	This ship can mount High House Multimodal Armor configurations. With an adaptor, it can also utilize Predecessor Multimode Armor materials.

variants.name: Heron (Author's Revenge)
variants.description: The Heron is the Remnant's ultimate last resort: Flight. These mobile starports are built to serve as the core elements of evacuation fleets when the Remnant are ultimately pushed to the brink of destruction in their home systems. These massive ships are capable of lifting enormous amounts of resources and operate both in space and on land, and are continuously updated to make full use of the latest technological innovations. 	The few Herons in existence are carefully guarded secrets that embody the Remnant's core tactics of speed, stealth, and survival. Given the tiny number that exist, they are never available for discretionary use by Remnant captains and are always operated under the authority and direction of a prefect.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Peregrine (Author's Revenge)
variants.description: The Peregrine is the first capital warship designed by Taely using fresh insights garnered from recent experimentation as well as renewed studies of the void sprites. Encompassing over a century of development since the last generation of warships was built, it is the forerunner of a new breed of Remnant ships. 	The Peregrine was designed along the lines of old-earth's fast-attack cruisers. Drawing on inspiration from its namesake, famed for being the fastest self-propelled lifeform on Earth, it is designed to strike hard and fast. It closes quickly with enemies to unleash devastating barrages in the opening seconds of combat. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Peregrine's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Petrel (Author's Revenge)
variants.description: The Petrel is a multi-role mining/wing leader fightercraft designed to provide support for flights of lighter Terns in high-risk environments. The ship's design originated as an urban mobile gun platform that flitted around structures and natural terrain, but proved easy to adapt into a spacecraft. 	The Remnant are loath to sacrifice pilots and crew from the comparatively small pool they are drawn from. As such, their fighters are equipped with medium-range weaponry designed to strike enemies from afar. 	Fighters do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a fighter unless you have a ship in your fleet with a fighter bay.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Tern (Author's Revenge)
variants.description: The Tern is a small, hardy drone developed to plunge into the atmosphere of nearby gas giants for collecting valuable resources. These thick-shelled craft are also surprisingly effective when pressed into service as screening ships when enemies intrude into Remnant space. 	Unlike most spacefaring nations, the Remnant do not have enough people to pilot fighter wings in waves likely to sustain significant casualties. As such, they frequently use these hardy drones to fulfill similar screening roles in their home systems, allowing manned craft to focus on more specialized tasks. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay.

variants.name: Avlaki (Harvester)
variants.description: The Avlaki is a mid-sized freighter loosely descended from a pre-hyperdrive solar-electric tug design. Its low cost and renowned maintainability has enabled it to remain in service to this day, and is a popular choice among independent captains. 	Enterprising captains often exploit the commonality of the Koryfi and Avlaki designs, swapping out the standard cargo containers for a centrifuge habitat. 	While its standard set of magnetoplasmadynamic thrusters give it an acceleration generously described as sluggish, the Avlaki's constant thrust flight profile allows it to reach an impressive cruising velocity given enough time.

variants.name: Entasi (Harvester)
variants.description: The Entasi is a mid-sized mining vessel, immediately recognizable by its pair of huge solar thermal generators. With the power and weapons capacity needed to support laser mining weapons, the Entasi is able to quickly and efficiently cut through asteroids, whose mineral contents can then be collected by the swarm of Sonikis cargo drones it can carry into an asteroid field. 	While somewhat fragile, the energy and space available to the Entasi can make it a potent warship with the right modifications. Rumors abound that certain Entasi captains sympathetic to the Dissonance movement maintain a stockpile of weapons for this very eventuality.

variants.name: Modified Tachytia (Harvester)
variants.description: This was once an Avgi sublight starship, one of the last models built before the discovery of the hyperdrive. Most starships around this period used ram-augmented fusion drives to reach cruising speeds of up to 0.25c, but the Tachytia class was designed to reach a velocity of 0.4c with an antimatter fuel source to ignite propellant gathered with its huge ramscoop. 	This particular ship was never launched on its mission, commissioned just before the hyperdrive made it obsolete. Now, it has been extensively modified by removing many of its propellant tanks, replacing them with a hyperdrive, additional equipment spaces, and several docking bays. The cryosleep bay has also been substituted for spacious habitatation cylinders, making this a true city ship.

variants.name: Polari (Harvester)
variants.description: The Polari-class Scout is a legacy design that has managed to remain relevant in the current era by virtue of fulfilling a role historically not requiring much in the way of combat power. A specialized science ship, it is fitted with a spacious laboratory for analyzing samples and processing data, as well as an extensive suite of sensor arrays for recording observations. A pair of bays can deploy Optikon sensor drones, while an external mount is designed to hold an Akoustiki Excursion Vehicle for piloted sample gathering operations. 	Despite this versatility, the contested battlespace of the post-Incursion Avgi cluster is one in which the Polari is simply not as capable in. As science crews are increasingly asked to lead risky scouting expeditions back to the Avgi homeworld, demands for a newer, more survivable science ship routinely make their way to the Twilight Guard.

EventFleetChanges: Adds fleet in "Gossamer" via event "midnight avgi gossamer harvesters" (rate 40000)

variants.name: Undsyni (Harvester)
variants.description: The Undsyni-class Auxiliary Freighter is not a flimsy bulk freighter, but rather one built to be large and strong enough to hold its own against attacks from smaller, more militarized vessels. While not quite as payload efficient as more spindly ships such as the Avlaki and Harmonikos, the Undsyni's resilience makes it much more survivable against attacks, with its fusion torch giving it the acceleration to both evade enemies and minimize travel times. 	Even before the Incursion, the Undsyni's strong hull and internal outfit capacity made it a popular option as a capital ship for renegade groups who could not gain access to specialized warships. 	A reinforced spine running the length of the ship allows it to fit a huge Plasmadyne Scoop, capable of bearing the extreme stresses the plasma magnet's field inflicts on its superconducting magnets. In this configuration, a tanker Undsyni can supply the fuel needs of an entire fleetgroup across dozens of systems.

variants.name: Akoustiki (Harvester)
variants.description: The Akoustiki Excursion Vehicle is a modern take on the utility pod, a small personal craft designed to aid in the maintenance and repair of a station, or a carrier vessel and its escorts. It is just as commonly seen flitting about the orbitals as it is servicing satellites or acting as a personal transport shuttle between stations and low gravity bodies. Recent advances in magnetoplasmadynamic engines have made it a capable mining craft as well, albeit one with little cargo space for ores. 	Fighters do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a fighter unless you have a ship in your fleet with a fighter bay.

variants.name: Sonikis (Harvester)
variants.description: The Sonikis Utility Drone was built as a cheap interorbital cargo drone, originally designed to carry modular cargo containers between stations and small moons. It is now commonly used by large freighters to assist in loading and unloading cargo, as well as to collect ores while asteroid mining. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay.

variants.name: Heliarch Judicator (Rogue)
variants.description: During their time battling the Quarg, the Coalition focused on producing the strongest, toughest warships they could, so fightercraft were out of the question. Now, however, the Heliarch's shield matrix and hull integrity technology is much more advanced, and they have recently experimented with such ships. The Judicator was made for transportation of these new fighters. 	Alongside their six fighter bays, Judicators come with a large bunk count and higher cargo space than other Heliarch warships, thus doubling as a logistics vessel for transporting troops and equipment.

variants.name: Luminazoa Specimen
variants.description: The exposed mantle of Hell's Maw is home to a thriving colony of these creatures. While they are content to harmlessly scavenge for minerals, they can become dangerous when provoked. Their tendrils are able to emit electrical bursts which can disrupt a ship's power systems.
governmentEvents: Event "korath hunting": Korath attitude toward Indigenous Lifeform → -0.01

variants.name: Ionic Leech Specimen
variants.description: These creatures have infested the Northern Passage since before humans colonized the north. They crave the power generated by ships and are somehow able to consume it through the use of organs uniquely evolved for the task. While they're a rare sight, captains who have the misfortune of encountering them will find that they attack in large swarms.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Indigenous Predator → -0.01

variants.name: Astero Nautilus Specimen
variants.description: The Astero Nautilus lurk amongst the asteroids of Pebble Beach. Their rock-like shells are hardened from centuries of consuming the minerals in the surrounding asteroids.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Indigenous Predator → -0.01

variants.name: Plasma Parasite Specimen
variants.description: While these creatures are neither aggressive nor malicious, the Heliarchs consider them a nuisance. They are attracted to the exhaust emissions of starship engines and will swarm over a ship. Unfortunately 90% of their bodies consist of volatile plasma, causing them to explode violently when exposed to weapons fire.

variants.name: Nova Firefly Specimen
variants.description: An invasive species from beyond our galaxy. These creatures thrive in the super heated gasses of dissipating supernovas. Through an unknown process, they are able to produce a fiery burst of their own flames.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Invasive Lifeform → -0.01

variants.name: Star Gazer Specimen
variants.description: An invasive species from beyond our galaxy. They seem possessed by an insatiable curiosity, observing everything they encounter with multiple eyes and other, more alien, sensory organs. While not particularly aggressive, Stargazers can be dangerous if provoked. Their bodies are covered with sharp quills that can be flung towards predators. They regenerate quickly, allowing them to maintain a constant stream of fire. These projectiles are made of a material that evades detection by anti-missile systems and may have other unknown properties.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Invasive Lifeform → -0.01

variants.name: Subsidurial Tamed
variants.description: It is unclear what these creatures are, where they come from, or how they evolved. Scientists have dissected several, but so far the results have simply been that these creatures contain no materials or resources of value; are not even slightly edible, and are too big to be kept as pets. 	To date, none have demonstrated any sign of sapience, and the few captains who have seen them basically consider them to be the bison of space.

variants.name: Granofel (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: Unlike many Gegno ships that are capable in a variety of roles, Granofels were designed for the sole purpose of hauling huge loads of cargo; they lack bunks for anything beyond a proper crew, and are most often found freighting massive shipments of both raw and refined ore to and from mining industries. They can also be seen paired with a mining vessel to extend the duration of a mining run due to the higher cargo capacity. Apart from mining, Granofels are also used in transporting heavy materials needed to construct other large ships.

variants.name: Gypsum (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: To fuel their increasing need for materials, the Gegno designed a new ship class for the sole purpose of mining. The resulting platform, the Gypsum, is not much more than a flying drill with cargo containers, engines, and a bridge attached behind it, making it cost-efficient and easy to manufacture. 	Because Gegno engines are not very powerful, the Gypsum has difficulty chasing faster-moving asteroids. In order to alleviate this problem without needing to massively increase the engine space on the ship, the Gegno have instead developed the powerful Excavator Drill, which can shred asteroids in a matter of seconds, meaning the Gypsum only needs to be near an asteroid for a mere moment in order to mine it.

variants.name: Corundum (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: While the Gypsum has remained the most reliable mining platform for generations, the Corundum was designed for the purpose of modularity on account of the ever-growing technological potential of the Gegno. Using a similar principle to the Gypusm's design, the Corundum's structure is mostly built around not one but two adjustable drill systems that are capable of mounting more advanced mining tools. 	Although not able to mount the powerful Excavator Drill, the Corundum's engine capacity is twice that of the Gypsum, and the modularity of the two new mounting systems grants it the ability to adapt to future technologies that the Gegno may develop.

variants.name: Protolith (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: A relic from another age, Protoliths are the last of the Generation ships constructed by the Gegno to colonize the stars. Now that other more easily constructed and hyperdrive-capable transport ships are commonplace, Protoliths are no longer found in service, and the very few that are still functioning are either preserved as artifacts or seldom used as hauling vessels between planets of the Gegno home system of Heutesl.

variants.name: Schist (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: Based on the Gegno's old Dolomite, the Schist is a mid-range ship used by the Vi. It can carry a decent amount of cargo, and has enough bunks to carry a whole platoon of warriors. It is the primary vessel used to transport recruits to the front lines, and veterans back to home territories. 	Although is it lightly armed compared to other Vi ships, Schists still are mounted with a pair of forward facing cannons and a turret so they can bring some type of weaponry to any possible engagement, as well as a set of angled guns for deterring any smaller, faster ships from attempting to flank the vessel.

variants.name: Eclogite (Light Scrap)
variants.description: While the style of longer battleship-esque vessels is a Gegno Vi staple, another shipyard rose to the competition for Vi warship designs. The Eclogite is one of the newest designs in the Vi fleet - a gunboat armed to the teeth with cannons, and maneuverability that the Vi's larger ships lack. It plays the role of a hit-and-run vessel, unloading volleys of shells against a target's armor in a rapid maneuver before adjusting its position for another run.

variants.name: Hornfel (Heavy Scrap)
variants.description: Hornfels are the workhorse of the Gegno Vi's military - decently sized, decently fast, and more than decently armed warships designed for the frontline of operations. Hornfels are also the most configurable ship in the Vi's fleet, lined with many mounting points to support cargo pods, allowing them to provide a secondary transport role for when the Vi require replacement supplies in war. Other variants of Hornfels are instead occasionally found with adjustments to carry a larger armament. This multi-role function is extremely valued and is the reason why the Hornfel is one of the Vi's most popular ships.

variants.name: Gneiss (Light Scrap)
variants.description: Gneiss battleships are the Gegno Vi's true sword and shield in war. They are slightly older than the Hornfels and Schists, but carry the heaviest armament, bearing three huge mounts dedicated to holding enormous Ballistic Cannons. Gneiss also have extremely strong armor plating, and can take a hefty beating while firing threatening broadsides at the opposing force. 	Unfortunately, in exchange for huge firepower and defensive armor, they lack speed and maneuverability, even when fitted with the largest engine systems the Vi have to offer.

variants.name: Feldspar (Thermal Scrap)
variants.description: The mighty Feldspar is a Scin creation to behold. As a testbed for the new Halite fighters, Feldspars bring their own small fleets with them and overwhelm their enemy. They were also designed as a semi-experimental platform, built around a brand new multi-engine system and the latest in Gegno plasma technology. 	Able to keep a decent stance away from a battle while putting down artillery fire, Feldspars are quite a dangerously well-rounded ship for their size. On the downside, they are more susceptible to hull damage like any other Scin warship, especially when alone. As such, they rely on their fighters to keep their enemies at a distance.

variants.name: Epidote (Thermal Scrap)
variants.description: Epidotes are large independent research platforms with adequately-sized cargo holds, allowing them to perform as a reliable heavy freighter for the Gegno Scin. A large number of bunks either help transport groups of Scin scientists to their project destinations, or allow for mobile on-board demonstrations and observations. Each Epidote is equipped with a rear fighter docking bay capable of carrying two Halites, typically used to ship Halite fighters around Scin space to resupply carriers. Thanks to these fighters and the Epidotes' three dorsal turrets, they can also be used as a secondary warship when needed. 	Like other Gegno Scin ships, Epidotes themselves are an experimental test bed; they are built around the same large engine system tested on Feldspars, making them notably fast for their size.

variants.name: Kyanite (Thermal Scrap)
variants.description: Kyanites are intricately-built test platforms for Gegno Scin technology, equipped with an extensive built-in power system and energy reserve able to support many types of outfits. Weapon experimentation, the most common practice of Kyanites, is recorded by various scanner instruments littering the two long structures on the front of the hull. Despite being weapon research vessels, Kyanites are not combat-capable due to how exposed their systems are and how little hull covers them. These systems are also very expensive and difficult to produce, so only a small amount of Kyanites are found in service. 	The scanner system found on the Tridymite was originally developed and tested on Kyanite platforms, eventually becoming integrated into the hull as well.

variants.description: These sensor-laden exploration vessels hail back to a more peaceful era of the Hai. These expensive features are the reason the ship has been replaced with the Lightning Bug. However, this ship has seen combat in recent years against human pirates. With room for plentiful shield regeneration, good maneuverability, and the range to strike deep in pirate territory, their long sleep has ended.

variants.name: Scarab (Bloodstone)
variants.description: The hard-working cousin to the Lightning Bug, the Scarab has only ever grown in popularity, never declined. That this statistic is occasionally measured in thousandths of a percentage point for years at a time is immaterial to the title. This lightweight transport is commonly the pick for Grasshopper pilots looking to make money while continuing to feed their free spirit. It is also large enough to transport a large Hai family, making it perfect for nearly any odd job in Hai space.

variants.description: The Sea Scorpion was designed several decades ago to serve as a mobile platform to launch Trackers. While individually vulnerable, the reduced cost of manufacturing compared to Shield Beetles allow the materially inferior Unfettered to gain a numerical advantage against their brethren.

variants.name: Leviathan Test Dummy
variants.description: The Betelgeuse Shipyards Leviathan has been in service since long before the Republic existed. Although considered today to be an outdated and clunky model, it is still a force to be reckoned with.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Falcon Test Dummy
variants.description: The Tarazed Falcon is one of the most powerful warships that civilians can buy, a sleeker and more maneuverable alternative to the venerable and somewhat outdated Leviathan.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Firebird Test Dummy
variants.description: The Betelgeuse Shipyards Firebird is a warship with a long and storied past; Firebirds fought on both sides of the Alpha Wars over half a millennium ago, and although the equipment and systems have been upgraded continuously since then, the basic design remains almost the same. The Firebird is also a very rugged ship and easy to repair; supposedly a few of the Firebirds that fought in those wars are still in service today.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Berserker Test Dummy2
variants.description: Once one of the most popular interceptor-class ships, the Berserker's popularity is now waning in favor of more modern and versatile ships like the Hawk. Although limited numbers are still produced by Betelgeuse Shipyards, most Berserkers that are in service today are more than half a century old.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Quicksilver Test Dummy2
variants.description: The Megaparsec Quicksilver is a warship built around a single concept: to design the smallest and fastest ship capable of carrying two Particle Cannons. Because of its speed, reverse thrusters, and long weapons range, the Quicksilver can keep a safe distance from most targets and bombard them with particle bursts until they are destroyed. The focus on its weaponry left the Quicksilver with no room for even the most basic shield generator. Unfortunately the Headhunter eventually surpassed the original design intent, but the Quicksilver's better durability to cost ratio, and the existence of long-term contracts, has kept it in use with Syndicate security forces.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Splinter Test Dummy2
variants.description: The Splinter is the largest warship produced by the Megaparsec shipyard. It is designed to be faster and more maneuverable than other ships of a similar size, in order to serve as a heavy escort ship or as part of a planetary defense and patrol fleet. Because of its intended use in merchant convoys, it also has a fair amount of cargo space.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Vanguard Test Dummy2
variants.description: The Vanguard is Syndicated Systems' newest warship intended for the heavy anti-pirate defense market. Vanguards offer an unusual feature set, focusing on powerful fixed guns and featuring Syndicated Systems' latest automation technologies, resulting in an atypically low crew complement for a ship its size. Few capital ships will endure for long under the withering fusillade of gunfire that it can unleash against those in front of it.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Mule Test Dummy
variants.description: The Mule is as much of a hodgepodge as its looks suggest. The Lionheart ship designers combined a good deal of cargo space with a decent amount of weaponry and even a fighter bay, and ended up with a ship that is mostly used as a freighter but can also be used as a warship because of its heavy armament and shields. This hodgepodge nature has its downside, though, namely its high crew requirement and the fact that any dedicated ship of the same cost will do better in a specialized role than the Mule will.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Hauler Test Dummy
variants.description: Several centuries ago, in the early days of the Republic, the sudden increase in commerce and space travel led to high demand for cargo ships. Haulers were first created simply by bolting a cockpit and engine block onto a cargo container, and the basic design has not changed much since then.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Freighter Test Dummy
variants.description: The Freighter is designed by the Syndicate to be an efficient means of carrying cargo from system to system, but is so slow and difficult to land that most pilots hate flying them. 	Freighters are an obvious target for pirates, but turn much too slowly to be able to bring any forward-facing guns to bear on an approaching enemy. As a result, the latest model of freighter is equipped only with turrets, including an anti-missile turret to prevent attackers from simply bombarding them into submission from a safe distance.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Argosy Test Dummy
variants.description: The Argosy from Southbound Shipyards is very popular with merchants not because of its capacity, which is actually slightly smaller than the Syndicate Freighter, but because it can hold its own in combat even against a small pirate fleet. 	The Argosy is also a very easy ship to upgrade with faster engines or more powerful weapons as needed, so many privately owned Argosies have very different capabilities than the stock model.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Modified Argosy Test Dummy
variants.description: The Argosy has long been a favorite ship for pirates, who have come up with many tricks for modifying them to be more suitable as warships.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Phenomenon (dangerous) → -0.01

variants.name: Marauder Hauler (Relentless Grudge)
variants.description: Some Haulers are modified to reduce mass and drag by replacing the standard cargo container with something smaller. The previous owner of this Hauler took the standard Southbound Shipyards cargo container and cut it down to half its size.

variants.name: Liberator (Vindicator (Test))
variants.description: The Liberator is a new warship that was originally designed by Southbound Shipyards to replace the Skein. Rumor has it that the project scope shifted focus during development when a ship of alien origin was discovered at the edges of the Rim. As a result, the planned fighter bays were scrapped in favor of the concentrated fire mount. This design crams all of the ship's gun ports into a single central location, allowing multiple smaller guns to emulate the effect of having a single larger one. This negatively impacts the ship's cooling efficiency and increases the amount of work maintenance crews have to put in for guns not mounted on the edge of the firing cluster.

Named for a celebrated captain who gave her life to ensure her crippled vessel made it back to port with its desperately needed cargo of stolen fish, the Palavret-Class Raiding Ship continues that grim tradition. The spaceborne construction techniques employed allow for the ship's easy replacement, facilitating continued raids of nearby systems.

Every cabin has its own mini-bar, and the bathrooms have marble tile and showers that use actual hot water instead of chemicals or sonic vibrations. 	In support of environmental movements across the galaxy, all Star Queens come standard with an array of solar panels as their only source of energy as opposed to more popular power generators such as fuel cells or nuclear reactors that produce some amount of waste. variants.name: Sunracer (Modified Flivver)
variants.description: The ship of choice for most professional racing pilots. With a focus on maximizing speed, a Sunracer lacks space to spare for ubiquitous things like cargo, bunks, weapons, or a hyperdrive. 	These ships serve a unique niche and are exclusively sold at inflated prices on the planet they're named after. Although it's possible to squeeze one into a fighter bay, the prohibitive cost and minimal combat capability means there isn't a compelling reason to use them in that capacity.

variants.name: Liberator (Vindicator)
variants.description: The Liberator is a new warship that was originally designed by Southbound Shipyards to replace the Skein. Rumor has it that the project scope shifted focus during development when a ship of alien origin was discovered at the edges of the Rim. As a result, the planned fighter bays were scrapped in favor of the concentrated fire mount. This design crams all of the ship's gun ports into a single central location, allowing multiple smaller guns to emulate the effect of having a single larger one. This negatively impacts the ship's cooling efficiency and increases the amount of work maintenance crews have to put in for guns not mounted on the edge of the firing cluster.

variants.name: Plexus (Korath)
variants.description: The Plexus is a new warship that was originally designed by Southbound Shipyards to replace the Skein. There were rumors that an alternative design substituting the fighter launch bay with a massive gun mount was being considered. But if that were true, it's no surprise that the carrier version won out. Cynical observers of starship sales trends often mention that selling carriers gives Southbound a steady market for replacement fighters.

But some of these attempts manage to find a niche. Over half the passenger space on this Hogshead has been gutted to make room for more shield emitters and weapon systems to power the two additional gun ports. Thick armored plating has been welded over the passenger viewports and other vulnerable areas of the hull, making the ship heavier, but more durable.

variants.name: Modified Dromedary (Metro)
variants.description: The Tycho Crater Cooperative's Dromedary was one of the foremost colonization ships during the early era before piracy became rampant and triggered the necessity for city-ships to be more combat-oriented. These ships incorporate extensive hydroponics, large construction equipment installations, and hundreds of densely packed "dream cells" built to transport people in bulk. 	Since the Remnant do not have schematics for the Dromedary, just the highly-modified example of the Shattered Light, this ship is actually a commemorative replica of that specific ship. As such, it combines the original's odd mix of eclectic modifications with new Remnant systems. 	Unfortunately, since they lack the manufacturing facilities that would normally support a large construction project, it will cost massively more than it would have originally back on Luna.

variants.name: Barb (Lovelace)
variants.description: Though the Syndicate doesn't build fighter carriers, it is testing the waters with the Barb, a cheap and flexible carrier-launched craft featuring newly-developed miniaturized ion engines. The design philosophy of the Barb seems to have been "uglier than the Protector," and as you look at the cockpit nestled between the massive gun port and turret mount, you wonder where the power systems are supposed to go. Though an awkward-looking ship, it seems flexible enough to become a dangerous addition to any fleet with carriers. 	In order to be capable of fitting a Proton Gun while still maintaining a turret mount, Syndicated Systems had to remove various life support systems, requiring that the pilot wear a pressurized suit rather than having the cabin be fully pressurized. Although it makes piloting a Barb an uncomfortable experience, the result is a level of short-range firepower that is unheard of for a craft its size. 	Fighters do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a fighter unless you have a ship in your fleet with a fighter bay.

variants.name: Buckler (Hai)
variants.description: Built upon a Dagger chassis, the Buckler plays a very different combat role from its smaller sibling. Lacking any weapon mounts, it features a high number of shield emitters and some of the toughest hull armor of any interceptor in the galaxy. 	Buckler pilots are expected to prioritize the defense of the flagship they are meant to protect over their own safety. To encourage this, new Bucklers purchased from Lionheart include a free training video installed on the ship's computer. Mixed in with tutorials for operating and maintaining the spacecraft are inspirational stories praising heroic pilots who sacrificed themselves for the greater good.

variants.name: Bulk Freighter (hai drones)
variants.description: The Bulk Freighter is the ultimate cargo ship, able to carry as much cargo as four ordinary Syndicate Freighters. Its on-board gearing allows it to service even the most primitive colonies, though dock workers in busier spaceports often joke that it would be simpler to carry smaller freighters within its gigantic holds. 	It is also an incredibly slow and difficult to maneuver ship, especially when loaded down with cargo. Some freight caravans use ordinary freighters instead of Bulk Freighters just to avoid the hassle of constantly having to wait for the Bulk Freighter to properly align itself for hyperspace travel.

variants.name: Enforcer (Modified Blaster)
variants.description: Prior to the formation of the galactic Republic, many star systems were owned by "governing corporate entities," with the vast majority of space being inaccessible to private citizens. The only exception to this rule were the pirate bands, whose few ships were often stolen or rebellious corporate fleets of their own, yet who had an outsized impact on interstellar trade. The necessity for corporations to protect their operations meant that Enforcer was one of the most common vessels used for security and defense. The ship boasts an armament of four gun ports and a turreted mount, all packed on a small but defensible frame that was powerful for its time. 	Although no longer on the market, the Enforcer finds itself in the possession of a small number of merchants and, ironically, various groups of pirates, as an aging combat ship easily outperformed by other light warships or even interceptors of a similar size.

variants.name: Hogshead (Hijacked)
variants.description: First manufactured by a forgotten shipyard many centuries ago, the Hogshead got its iconic name from the keg-like shape of its engine pods; its design was a hot topic of discussion for captains everywhere. The ship quickly became popular after first being released for consumer purchase and was commonly seen around various systems as the go-to "space bus" in human space. 	Unfortunately, only a few decades after introducing the ship, the shipyard went bankrupt and was never heard from again, leaving the Hogshead to history as their one-hit-wonder. In the current era, Hogsheads are much less common; they are considered "unsightly" compared to modern vessels such as the Star Queen, though a few places in human space still sell them.

variants.name: Manta (Korath)
variants.description: After their Quicksilver light warship with its armament of Particle Cannons became a large success with convoy escorts and planetary defense forces, Megaparsec decided to develop a larger ship with similar maneuverability but heavier firepower. The Manta is the result: a ship with enough long-range firepower that fleeing from a battle with it is almost impossible.

variants.name: Mega Freighter (Blaster)
variants.description: The Syndicate's Mega Freighter is being marketed as a symbol for a new era of peace and prosperity in the post-war galaxy. Despite having double the cargo capacity of a Container Transport, the empty hull isn't much heavier unless it's carrying a full cargo load. In addition to the extra cargo space, this ship offers more flexibility for installing engines, weapons, and other outfits.

This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Plunder (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: This ship is exclusively for sale to certain members of the Covert Mining Cartel. The Plunder is often mistaken for a modification of the Sunder currently sold by Syndicate Shipyards. But its lineage can be traced back to an older model that ceased production long ago. 	This confusion is exacerbated by the fact that the Plunder is indeed missing two of its original external cargo pods. However, these pods were located in the ship's undercarriage. Their removal allowed installation of a second drone bay. Unlike the second drone on the Syndicate's Sunder, this one faces forward, allowing it to quickly target the Plunder's prey.

variants.name: Saber (Energy Cannons)
variants.description: During the caravan era, a boom of economic development spread along the paths of more heavily armed and technologically advanced merchant fleets originating from the Deep, which resulted in ships such as the Saber being developed. This medium warship was one of the powerhouses of military might in its time, armed to the teeth with five gun ports in the nose and a dorsal turret mount to fire at anything not in front of it. As pirates began to join together in larger war bands in response to the more heavily defended merchants, the Saber became popular amongst them as well. Unlike other ships such as the Firebird, it slowly faded out as competition rose, but it is nevertheless cherished by those who still own one.

variants.description: Rather than being a specific model of ship, the Scrappers are instead a family of vessels cobbled together from the remains of broken shuttles. Despite this, these ships are where many captains (and pirates) from poorer backgrounds get their start.

variants.name: Shuttle (Derelict)
variants.description: Although Betelgeuse Shipyards produces other ship models as well, the majority of their profits come from sales of the Shuttle. This versatile ship serves equally well as a passenger transport or a cargo courier. It also happens to be the cheapest ship you can buy which is capable of hyperspace travel. 	Shuttles are not designed to withstand combat of any sort, but they are fast and maneuverable enough to get out of harm's way if attacked by a larger, slower ship. Although they are typically unarmed, they have enough space for one weapon, which is the origin of the popular phrase, "as useless as a blaster cannon on a shuttlecraft."

variants.name: Sliver (Smuggler)
variants.description: The Sliver was Megaparsec's attempt to enter the luxury space liner market. While it is no longer sold at their main shipyards, some Paradise Worlds keep them in stock for their wealthy clientel. Despite a superficial resemblance to the Splinter, the Sliver is notable for its distinctive ability to have up to three yachts dock with it. 	(These yachts are sold separately.)

variants.name: Sparrow (Afterburner)
variants.description: Classified as an interceptor rather than a fighter because it has its own hyperdrive instead of needing to be carried inside a larger ship, the Tarazed Sparrow is the smallest and cheapest combat ship available. Because of its limited cargo and passenger space, the primary way for a Sparrow pilot to pay the bills is to upgrade the weapons and hunt pirates... or become one. In either case, it is a perilous way to earn a living. 	Government reports indicate that as many as two out of every three first-time ship buyers who choose to pilot a Sparrow lose their ship (and often, their life as well) within the first month of owning it. Pilots who have survived longer than that tend to swear by replacing the stock weapons with missile launchers.

variants.description: Classified as an interceptor rather than a fighter because it has its own hyperdrive instead of needing to be carried inside a larger ship, the Tarazed Sparrow is the smallest and cheapest combat ship available. Because of its limited cargo and passenger space, the primary way for a Sparrow pilot to pay the bills is to upgrade the weapons and hunt pirates... or become one. In either case, it is a perilous way to earn a living. 	Government reports indicate that as many as two out of every three first-time ship buyers who choose to pilot a Sparrow lose their ship (and often, their life as well) within the first month of owning it. Pilots who have survived longer than that tend to swear by replacing the stock weapons with missile launchers.

variants.name: Sparrow (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: Classified as an interceptor rather than a fighter because it has its own hyperdrive instead of needing to be carried inside a larger ship, the Tarazed Sparrow is the smallest and cheapest combat ship available. Because of its limited cargo and passenger space, the primary way for a Sparrow pilot to pay the bills is to upgrade the weapons and hunt pirates... or become one. In either case, it is a perilous way to earn a living. 	Government reports indicate that as many as two out of every three first-time ship buyers who choose to pilot a Sparrow lose their ship (and often, their life as well) within the first month of owning it. Pilots who have survived longer than that tend to swear by replacing the stock weapons with missile launchers.

variants.description: The Syndicate CT-50 Star Barge is little more than a cluster of cargo containers with an engine at one end and a cockpit on the other. It is a slow and ugly ship, but it can carry enough cargo to earn its captain a steady income even in parts of the galaxy where it is hard to find passengers to carry or courier missions. 	Because they often carry valuable cargo, and because they are too slow to evade any attackers, Star Barges are a common target of pirates.

variants.name: Star Queen (Advanced Research)
variants.description: The Star Queen is a relic of a more peaceful period of galactic history: a luxury liner for high-end tourists. Every cabin has its own mini-bar, and the bathrooms have marble tile and showers that use actual hot water instead of chemicals or sonic vibrations. 	In support of environmental movements across the galaxy, all Star Queens come standard with an array of solar panels as their only source of energy as opposed to more popular power generators such as fuel cells or nuclear reactors that produce some amount of waste. Although some argue that this is a pointless move given the prevalence of clean fusion reactors, others have applauded it and cited the prohibitive costs of fusion reactors as a reason for using solar panels.

variants.name: Quicksilver (Korath)
variants.description: The Megaparsec Quicksilver is a warship built around a single concept: to design the smallest and fastest ship capable of carrying two Particle Cannons. Because of its speed, reverse thrusters, and long weapons range, the Quicksilver can keep a safe distance from most targets and bombard them with particle bursts until they are destroyed. The focus on its weaponry left the Quicksilver with no room for even the most basic shield generator. Unfortunately the Headhunter eventually surpassed the original design intent, but the Quicksilver's better durability to cost ratio, and the existence of long-term contracts, has kept it in use with Syndicate security forces.

variants.description: The technology on the Volary, while in line with other modern ships, is surprisingly mundane for a newly constructed ship from Lionheart. This has caused some to speculate that the Deep has lost their edge in technological advancement. Alternatively, conspiracy theorists suggest that the Deep has been sitting on this design for some time and has only revealed it now in preparation for some threat unknown to the general public. Deep Security, for its part, has no comment on these rumors.

variants.name: Bulk Freighter(hai)
variants.description: The Bulk Freighter is the ultimate cargo ship, able to carry as much cargo as four ordinary Syndicate Freighters. Its on-board gearing allows it to service even the most primitive colonies, though dock workers in busier spaceports often joke that it would be simpler to carry smaller freighters within its gigantic holds. 	It is also an incredibly slow and difficult to maneuver ship, especially when loaded down with cargo. Some freight caravans use ordinary freighters instead of Bulk Freighters just to avoid the hassle of constantly having to wait for the Bulk Freighter to properly align itself for hyperspace travel.

variants.name: Missileboat (Rainmaker (Nuclear))
variants.description: For centuries, the Missileboat provided fleet admirals with a reliable artillery unit to support their front line vessels. The outdated systems interface on this ship have a higher crew requirement than the Rainmaker currently used by the Navy. Retired Missileboats are sometimes used by bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Scrapper (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: Rather than being a specific model of ship, the Scrappers are instead a family of vessels cobbled together from the remains of broken shuttles. On the rare occasion that Republic authorities bother to recognize their existence, Scrappers are treated as almost-illegal, patent-infringing death traps. Despite this, these ships are where many captains (and pirates) from poorer backgrounds get their start.

variants.name: Scrounger (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: Assembled from the burned out remains of wrecked freighters, Scroungers are how some pilots lacking the funds for better options begin their careers. Unfortunately, it is not uncommon for those facing financial desperation to turn to small scale acts of piracy, scavenging parts and cargo from the scraps leftover by larger raiders.

variants.name: Starcadia (Prototype)
variants.description: The technology on the Starcadia, while in line with other modern ships, is surprisingly mundane for a newly deployed ship from the Deep. This has caused some to speculate that the Deep has lost their edge in technological advancement. Alternatively, conspiracy theorists suggest that the Deep has been sitting on this design for some time and is only releasing it now in preparation for some threat unknown to the general public. Deep Security, for its part, has no comment on these rumors.

variants.name: Enforcer (Used)
variants.description: Prior to the formation of the galactic Republic, many star systems were owned by "governing corporate entities," with the vast majority of space being inaccessible to private citizens. The only exception to this rule were the pirate bands, whose few ships were often stolen or rebellious corporate fleets of their own, yet who had an outsized impact on interstellar trade. The necessity for corporations to protect their operations meant that Enforcer was one of the most common vessels used for security and defense. The ship boasts an armament of four gun ports and a turreted mount, all packed on a small but defensible frame that was powerful for its time. 	Although no longer on the market, the Enforcer finds itself in the possession of a small number of merchants and, ironically, various groups of pirates, as an aging combat ship easily outperformed by other light warships or even interceptors of a similar size.

variants.name: Modified Hogshead (Used)
variants.description: Occasionally a pirate gets the idea in his head to adapt a ship not designed for warfare into a pirate vessel. Oftentimes the results weren't worth the effort. But some of these attempts manage to find a niche. A Modified Hogshead might appear under the command of bounty hunters or slavers who are likely to find a ship of this type useful in their line of work. 	Over half the passenger space on this Hogshead has been gutted to make room for more shield emitters and weapon systems to power the two additional gun ports. Thick armored plating has been welded over the passenger viewports and other vulnerable areas of the hull, making the ship heavier, but more durable.

variants.name: Saber (Used)
variants.description: During the caravan era, a boom of economic development spread along the paths of more heavily armed and technologically advanced merchant fleets originating from the Deep, which resulted in ships such as the Saber being developed. This medium warship was one of the powerhouses of military might in its time, armed to the teeth with five gun ports in the nose and a dorsal turret mount to fire at anything not in front of it. As pirates began to join together in larger war bands in response to the more heavily defended merchants, the Saber became popular amongst them as well. Unlike other ships such as the Firebird, it slowly faded out as competition rose, but it is nevertheless cherished by those who still own one.

variants.name: Far'itar (Jump)
variants.description: Dedicated cargo transports are no longer necessary among the Korath Exiles. Rather than being scrapped, these ships have been repurposed to serve as mobile prisons. Criminals convicted of serious crimes are given a choice between a quick death via a microbot nutrigel processor or a life long assignment working on a Far'itar mining vessel. Prisoners who fail to perform their duties are still eligible for being tossed into the nutrigel processor. 	Operating these vessels can be lucrative for its captains, but the Korath authorities require them to activate their self destruct in the event of a mutiny or other event that could result in a prisoner escape. Whether or not they have the fortitude to fulfill this duty is put to the test whenever they engage in a boarding battle.

variants.name: Ikatila'ej (Thermal Obliterator)
variants.description: For most of their manufacturing needs, the Korath rely, as even some terrestrial species do, upon their space station and asteroid infrastructure. Due to their spacebound existence, however, the acceptability for failure and downtime is slim to nonexistent. Should equipment aboard a station or a world-ship fail, the Ikatila'ej, named for an inventor famously proficient in a variety of fields, is called in to provide critical support. Its microbot-run factory produces basic living supplies, machine parts, and systems cores, and may assist in continuing stalled production. 	When not assisting with damaged ships and stations, or replenishing its own stores, the Ikatila'ej serves as an all-in-one recycling, mining, refining, and factory ship, using its microbot-powered grinder to rapidly turn asteroids and garbage into whatever products the civilian economic planning committees have determined to be in the most dire need.

variants.name: Korsmanath A'awoj (Jump)
variants.description: Korsmanath A'awojs, named in memory of the Korath home system, are massive nomadic habitats that hold much of their remaining population. True flying cities, they could be self-contained miniature worlds were it not for their heavy defensive armament and reliance on unsustainable materials, methods, and sources of power. 	Commission of new Korsmanath A'awojs is a resource-demanding, labor-intensive, painstaking process fraught with political intrigue. Navarchs fight with the civilian government for resources and yard time they would rather devote to building raiding and defensive fleets, civilians vie with each other for a place on the next ship, and planning committees argue with engineers over what methods and technologies to use. This leads to construction delays, corner-cutting, and over-militarization of the design at best, and violent feuds at worst.

variants.name: Palavret (Korath Raider (Fireswarm))
variants.description: Successive raider designs have been the Korath warship of choice for plundering neighboring species for generations. Named for a celebrated captain who gave her life to ensure her crippled vessel made it back to port with its desperately needed cargo of stolen fish, the Palavret-Class Raiding Ship continues that grim tradition. 	Like all Exile ships, the Palavret has been adapted to house as many Korath as possible, as comfortably as possible, inflating its size beyond similarly armed warships. The spaceborne construction techniques employed allow for the ship's easy replacement, facilitating continued raids of nearby systems.
